hints: Set $y = 0$ in the curve equation $y = x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x$.
walkthrough:
Set $y = 0$ to find where the curve crosses the $x$-axis:
$$x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x = 0$$

hints: The total shaded area is the sum of the area above the $x$-axis from $0$ to $1$ and the absolute area below the $x$-axis from $1$ to $3$.
Evaluate on $[0, 1]$ to get $\frac{5}{12}$ and on $[1, 3]$ to get $-\frac{8}{3}$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the upper region from $x = 0$ to $x = 1$:
$$\text{Area}_1 = \left( \frac{1}{4}(1) - \frac{4}{3}(1) + \frac{3}{2}(1) \right) - 0 = \frac{3 - 16 + 18}{12} = \frac{5}{12}$$

Evaluate the lower region from $x = 1$ to $x = 3$:
$$\text{Area}_2 = \left[ \frac{1}{4}x^4 - \frac{4}{3}x^3 + \frac{3}{2}x^2 \right]_1^3 = \left( \frac{81}{4} - \frac{4}{3}(27) + \frac{3}{2}(9) \right) - \frac{5}{12}$$
$$\text{Area}_2 = \left( \frac{81}{4} - 36 + \frac{27}{2} \right) - \frac{5}{12} = -\frac{9}{4} - \frac{5}{12} = -\frac{32}{12} = -\frac{8}{3}$$

Sum the absolute values to find the total shaded area:
$$\text{Total Area} = \frac{5}{12} + \left|-\frac{8}{3}\right| = \frac{5}{12} + \frac{32}{12} = \frac{37}{12} \quad \left(\approx 3.08\right)$$

ai_rubric.Finding Areas Under Curves: Integrates correctly to $\frac{1}{4}x^4 - \frac{4}{3}x^3 + \frac{3}{2}x^2$ (B2). Evaluates on $[0,1]$ to get $\frac{5}{12}$ (M1, A1). Evaluates on $[1,3]$ to get $-\frac{8}{3}$ (M1, A1). Sums positive areas to obtain $\frac{37}{12}$ (A1).
